CFML Language Reference: Functions

Chr

Returns a one-character string for a character code from 0 to 255.

Category

String functions

Syntax

Chr(number)

Parameters

number
A character code from 0 to 255.

Returns

A string containing that one character. Chr(0) returns an empty string.

Usage

Chr is the usual way to put characters into a string that are awkward to type in a CFML expression: Chr(13) & Chr(10) is a carriage return/line feed pair (needed between e-mail headers), Chr(9) is a tab and Chr(34) a double quote. Asc converts the other way.

Example

Opens the example in a new window. The example runs on this server, so it only works when you browse from the server itself (127.0.0.1).
<CFSET CRLF = Chr(13) & Chr(10)>
<CFOUTPUT>
<P>Codes 65 to 74 spell:
<CFLOOP INDEX="i" FROM="65" TO="74">#Chr(i)#</CFLOOP></P>
<P>A quote in a string: He said #Chr(34)#Hello#Chr(34)#</P>
<P>Length of a CR/LF pair: #Len(CRLF)# characters</P>
</CFOUTPUT>

See also

Asc, StripCR, RepeatString
